_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for F retrospectives (retro/build_f.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date: a filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern). Ford's earnings 8-Ks of 2021-2026 were accepted after the close (16:07-16:14 ET) and its 10-Qs and 10-Ks the same evenings, so a print, its 10-Q or 10-K, and a Q4 print's 10-K share one date. Generated by a script from row strings of the filings (each checked with retro/tools/verbatim.py); every growth rate, margin change and rule-T value is computed. See retro/README.md, 'F'. The early era (dates before 2022-01-01, retro/README.md 'F 2008-2011') has its own records: the Q4 releases of 2001-2006 for the EPS history, the 10-Ks of FY2000-FY2010 (and the FY2005 10-K/A), the earnings releases of Q2 2007 to Q3 2011 (accepted before the open; a Q4 print carries its year's actuals, fy_actual, until the 10-K), the 2011-12-08 dividend 8-K, and rule_t_r2008 (the 1997-2006 decade).

rule_t._doc: Rule T values behind the engine's signal thresholds (retro/README.md, 'F'): the decade of the FY2020 10-K, the vintage public on 2022-01-07, is 2011-2020. Each change comes from the latest 10-K published by then that reports both years, as a filing tabulates it (no sums, no narrative-derived levels); a measure the filings report for fewer years takes the changes they report (the AVGO rule). XBULL best, BULL median, BASE worst, BEAR one median-to-worst step beyond the worst.

rule_t_r2008._doc: Rule T values behind the 2008-era engine's thresholds (retro/README.md, 'F 2008-2011'): the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04, is 1997-2006.
